newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher after July CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher after July CPI.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday in active trading as the market showed relief after a low July consumer price index, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.17 pct to 111.45
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.2 pct to 111.77
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.25 pct to 110.67
* Dollar-linked government bonds: -0.18 pct at 110.6
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 108.89
Volume including Makams was a moderate 170 million shekels.

"The market was afraid of a higher CPI. Now players are back buying all kinds of bonds -- CPI-linked and unlinked. Basically the CPI has made everyone happy," said Adam Reuter of the Financial Immunities consulting firm.
The July index, published on Friday, rose by 1.0 percent, at the low end of economists' expectations of a 1.0 to 1.2 percent rise. In June the CPI rose by 1.1 percent.
"Players had stopped buying, waiting for the CPI. But now they realise that they can continue to buy everything, which explains the rise in trading volume," Reuter said.

"Basically the CPI was good enough for traders to hold on to CPI-linked bonds and continue buying them, and good enough for other traders to hold unlinked bonds and continue buying them," Reuter said.
Prices for inflation-linked bonds fell most of last week on fears that a high July index would trigger an interest rate hike at the end of the month.

"Now the market is behaving as if there won't be an interest rate hike at the end of the month," said a trader for an institutional investor, referring to the higher prices for CPI-linked long bonds and unlinked bonds.

Many traders still fear that the Bank of Israel will raise rates 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point at the end of the month. But some traders said if so that it would be a one-off rise and not a change in the overall trend towards lower interest rates.
The base rate has been 12.7 percent since the middle of June.
"The market forecasts an inflation of 9.5 to 10 percent in the coming 12 months," Reuter said. That puts inflation inside the government's target of seven to 10 percent.

Prices of dollar-linked bonds fell on Sunday after the dollar weakened against the shekel on Friday, Reuter said. On Friday the representative rate was fixed at 3.52 shekels to the dollar, against 3.529 shekels on Thursday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.52 shekels)
